validation.device: cargo xtask ailuros compile-tests <exported-project> produces an artifact marked tests. After separately authorized installation, read the ailuros-tests JSON result on UART at 115200 baud. Recompile with compile, then install the artifact marked workflow to resume normal operation.
validation.test_configuration: CONFIG_UNITY_ENABLE_64BIT=y is required; firmware configuration rejects tests without it. Test objects are retained with WHOLE_ARCHIVE.
validation.camera: The lince-facade example ailuros_camera_check exercises actual JPEG decoding, two viewers, final-viewer idle and resuming capture against an explicitly selected local Cell. Stop other instances using that Cell before running it.
validation.verified_hardware: Historical baseline before the board-profile/build-configuration refactor: GOOUUU V1.5 N16R8 / OV2640 passed 15 firmware cases and 170 decoded 320x240 JPEG frames with viewer lifecycle, including wall USB power. The refactored source has not yet repeated SDK compilation or hardware tests.
validation.board_configuration: nix develop .#interface --command cargo test -p lince-ailuros --test board_configuration -- --ignored (requires CMake 3.19+)
validation.sdk_matrix: Export fresh esp32s3 and goouuu-esp32s3-cam-v1.5 projects. Compile workflow and test images for both. Switch camera -> base -> camera in one build directory and confirm PSRAM/clock settings follow the profile. Then compile workflow after compile-tests and verify test mode is OFF.

setup_notes: The default esp32s3 profile assumes at least 4 MiB flash and no PSRAM or camera. The verified goouuu-esp32s3-cam-v1.5 profile requires 16 MiB physical flash, octal PSRAM at 80 MHz and the measured OV2640 pin map. Flash installation retains the protected 4 MiB partition layout for both.
The GOOUUU profile selects an 8 MHz camera clock because 20 MHz stalled transport on the tested hardware. Other sensors/boards need an explicitly verified clock; it is not a global camera default.

cmake/board.cmake derives SDK defaults from board.json. SDK configuration lives under build/ and is selected by a digest of the board, default settings and dependency inputs, preventing stale memory/clock options after changing profiles. Persist intentional overrides in source, not generated SDK files.
Use the native IDE and Fiote to review editable firmware source, then compile and install through the same pipeline. Keep Wi-Fi credentials out of source and model context.
The ESP needs a reachable HTTPS/WSS Facade origin and trusted certificate; Cell identity is configured separately from its address.
USB is the supplied initial installation/provisioning path. Wireless provisioning and OTA are possible separate extensions, not implemented setup modes.
Wall USB power works independently of the setup computer; the selected Cell or gateway must remain available.
Keys currently use software storage. Secure boot, flash encryption and irreversible chip protections require a separate recovery design.
supported_targets: ESP32-S3 only. Other ESP SoCs require a separately implemented and tested adapter; a different chip string is rejected.

source_ownership.repository: Shared firmware components, workflows, hardware profiles, manifests/lockfiles, default settings, tests, licenses and resources. Public improvements to exported workspaces belong back here or in a separately versioned custom project.
source_ownership.private_installation: Wi-Fi credentials, device keys, destination Cell/Signal binding, TLS keys, raw flash backups and Cell snapshots stay outside source control. No installed-device identifiers or network credentials are needed to export or compile a starter.
source_ownership.generated: SDK configuration, fetched managed_components and build outputs are generated locally. Keep reviewed images plus source revision/profile/toolchain/hash as release artifacts rather than committing caches.
source_ownership.customization: Edit board.json for sensor wiring, PSRAM mode/clock and camera clock. Edit sdkconfig.defaults for common SDK options and workflow sources for behavior. Built-in profiles are selected through the native Create project buttons or xtask export/select-profile.
